findings.text: Association between one cgroup and one css set is represented by a small link object holding two pointers plus two list nodes, one anchored at the cgroup side and one at the css set side, allowing traversal from either end.

Migration task collection holds separate source and destination css set lists, a task count, the subsystem currently under treatment, a selector for which list is active, and cursor fields for the current set and task during iteration.

Migration context holds preloaded source and destination set lists used to make later migration atomic, an embedded task collection, and a bit mask of affected subsystems; helper initializers provide empty list heads and select the source list as the active list.
Threaded identity is expressed by domain pointer inequality: a css set is threaded when its domain pointer differs from itself, and a cgroup is threaded when its domain cgroup differs from itself.

Default hierarchy membership is a root pointer comparison against the default root. Effective subsystem selection walks ancestors until the subsystem bit appears in the group mask; the mask itself comes from the parent subtree mask intersected for threaded groups, or from the root mask at the top.

Css set identity combines subsystem state array equality, domain default cgroup equality, and ordered per hierarchy cgroup pointer equality, with the changing hierarchy expected to point at the new group and all other hierarchies unchanged. Lookup hashing folds subsystem state addresses and the result selects a hash bucket.

New css set creation reuses an existing matching set when found, otherwise builds a fresh object with self domain, empty task and link collections, copied subsystem template, per hierarchy links with default group recorded, hash insertion, per subsystem list linkage and reference acquisition, plus a follow up domain lookup and linkage when the default group is threaded.

Release notification is a single flag test on the cgroup flags. Version one availability combines a per subsystem disable bit mask with a check for absence of legacy file definitions while default files exist.

Root iteration is RCU based and asserts the cgroup mutex is held. Subsystem iteration scans the subsystem table by index up to the subsystem count. Cgroup to css set resolution from a task relies on the css set lock to freeze group membership without task locking.

Css set reference handling uses a fast path that returns unless the count would reach one, otherwise takes the css set IRQ spinlock and runs the locked release. Locked release asserts that lock, detaches subsystem nodes and releases subsystem references, removes the hash entry, unlinks and frees association links with live cgroup handling, handles threaded domain release, and defers final free through RCU.

Attach serialization always takes the CPU hotplug read lock and pairs it with an attach mode: none takes nothing further, global takes the global threadgroup write semaphore, per threadgroup takes the target signal write semaphore. Unlock releases in reverse order and warns on an unexpected mode.

Migration preparation asserts cgroup mutex, and source registration additionally asserts the css set lock. Finish asserts cgroup mutex and takes the css set lock while clearing migration pointers, reinitializing preload nodes and releasing preloaded references.

Migration proceeds from source collection to destination lookup to task snapshot and execution to cleanup. Dead sets are ignored, duplicate source registration is ignored, equal source and destination is treated as a no operation with both references dropped, and otherwise destination sets are preloaded while the subsystem difference mask accumulates.

Task snapshot for migration skips exiting tasks, requires task membership linkage, ignores tasks whose set has no recorded source, counts accepted tasks, advances task iterators past the moved task, transfers task linkage into the per set migration queue, and queues source and destination sets for iteration when first used.

Cross hierarchy attach walks every root under cgroup and global attach locks, resolves the source group for the from task under the css set lock, and attaches the target task into each hierarchy until failure.

Single group attach collects source sets over one thread or a whole thread group under the css set lock, then prepares destinations, executes migration, finishes preload state, and emits an attach trace on success.

Visible operations provided by these fragments include locked css set release, default hierarchy test, root relative task and set lookup, attach lock and unlock, attach of one task and of a task across all roots, migration orchestration and its add source, prepare destination and finish helpers, and CPU hotplug read lock and unlock.

Root relative lookup has three behaviors: initial set maps directly to the root group, default root uses a cached default pointer, and other roots scan association links. Without cgroup mutex the link may already be freed and the result may be absent, so callers without that mutex must handle an empty result.

Destruction warns if a threaded child list is unexpectedly non empty and warns when acquiring a live reference on a dead group. Migration registration warns on stale migration pointers or non empty migration queues, and destination preparation warns on conflicting destination linkage.
Version one pid list deferred destruction delay is defined as one timer tick interval.
